source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV site is swollen, cool, and pale. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop and restart at another site
Apply a warm pack and continue
questions.rationale: These are signs of infiltration; the IV is disconnected and restarted at a different site, and movement limited.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Disconnect the IV infusion and restart at a different site

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During IV therapy, a client has distended neck veins, high BP, and dyspnea. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: These are signs of circulatory overload; slow the rate, notify the doctor, and monitor.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Slow the rate of the infusion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV vein is red, warm, and tender. After stopping the IV, what should be applied?
questions.rationale: For superficial thrombophlebitis, discontinue the IV and apply warm moist compresses; avoid the vein.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Apply warm, moist compress to the affected site

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An air embolism is suspected during IV therapy. How should the client be positioned?
questions.rationale: The client is placed on the left side (often head down) to trap air in the right heart, and the doctor is notified.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Position the patient on left side lying

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A rapid IV push causes pounding headache, chills, and rapid pulse. What is this?
questions.rationale: Speed shock results from giving IV push drugs too rapidly.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Complications (PDF p. 31)
questions.quote: Speed shock — may result from administration of IV push medications rapidly

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which blood product is used to increase oxygen-carrying capacity?
questions.rationale: Packed RBCs increase oxygen-carrying capacity; platelets treat bleeding from low platelets; FFP provides clotting factors.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Products (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Packed RBC Used to increase oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which IV solution is the ONLY one given with blood?
questions.rationale: Only normal saline is given with blood; dextrose causes hemolysis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Blood (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: ONLY 0.9NaCl (NSS) should be administered with blood.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Within what time must a unit of blood be completely transfused?
questions.rationale: Transfusion should be completed within 4 hours of removal from refrigeration.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Blood (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Transfusion should be completed within 4 hours

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which needle size is usually used for blood transfusion?
questions.rationale: Blood is usually given through an 18–20 gauge needle or catheter.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Administering Blood (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Blood is usually administered through a #18- #20 gauge intravenous needle or catheter

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How long can blood stay at room temperature before starting the transfusion?
questions.rationale: Blood should be at room temperature no more than 30 minutes before infusion begins.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Transfusion (PDF p. 32)
questions.quote: Make sure that blood is left at room temperature for no more than 30 minutes before starting the infusion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When is the client watched MOST closely during a transfusion?
questions.rationale: Run blood slowly the first 15 minutes and observe closely, with VS 15 minutes after starting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Blood Transfusion (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: Observe the client closely for the first 5 to 15 minutes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client develops chills, back pain, and hypotension during a transfusion. What is the FIRST action?
questions.rationale: These suggest a hemolytic reaction; stop the transfusion, keep the line open with NS, and notify the doctor.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transfusion Reaction (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: Stop the transfusion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client gets mild itching and hives during a transfusion. Which reaction is this?
questions.rationale: Mild allergic reactions (to plasma proteins) cause flushing, itching, urticaria; slow or stop, notify, and give antihistamine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transfusion Reaction (PDF p. 33)
questions.quote: Clinical manifestations: flushing, itching, urticaria, bronchial wheezing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During a transfusion, an older client develops cough, crackles, and distended neck veins. How is he positioned?
questions.rationale: Circulatory overload: place upright with feet dependent, slow or stop, notify, and give diuretics and oxygen as ordered.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transfusion Reaction (PDF p. 34)
questions.quote: Place the patient upright with feet dependent

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An infection that results directly from a diagnostic or therapeutic procedure is:
questions.rationale: Iatrogenic infections result directly from procedures; endogenous come from the client's own flora.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Asepsis (PDF p. 34)
questions.quote: Latrogenic infection - direct result of diagnostic or therapeutic procedures

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which agent is used to clean blood spills?
questions.rationale: Chlorine (bleach) kills bacteria, TB, spores, fungi, and viruses and is used for blood spills.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Antiseptics and Disinfectants (PDF p. 34)
questions.quote: Used to clean blood spills

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What are standard autoclave conditions?
questions.rationale: Autoclaving uses steam under pressure at 15–17 lb and 121–123°C.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization (PDF p. 35)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sterilization method suits heat-sensitive items but is toxic to humans?
questions.rationale: Ethylene oxide penetrates well and suits heat-sensitive items but is toxic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sterilization (PDF p. 35)
questions.quote: Disadvantage: toxic to humans

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which body fluid is exempt from standard precautions?
questions.rationale: Standard precautions apply to blood, all body fluids, secretions, and excretions except sweat.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Standard Precautions (PDF p. 35)
questions.quote: Blood, all body fluids, secretions and excretions (except sweat)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which disease requires AIRBORNE precautions?
questions.rationale: Airborne precautions are for measles, varicella (including zoster), and pulmonary TB.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transmission-Based Precautions (PDF p. 36)
questions.quote: Ex: Measles (rubeola), Varicella, (including zoster), Pulmonary tuberculosis

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: A child has diphtheria. Which precautions are used?
questions.rationale: Droplet precautions apply to diphtheria, pertussis, mumps, rubella, strep pharyngitis, and pneumonic plague.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transmission-Based Precautions (PDF p. 36)
questions.quote: Example: diphtheria, mycoplasma pneumonia, pertussis, mumps, rubella

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which condition requires CONTACT precautions?
questions.rationale: Contact precautions apply to scabies, pediculosis, impetigo, C. difficile, hepatitis A, RSV, and MDROs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Transmission-Based Precautions (PDF p. 36)
questions.quote: impetigo, pediculosis, scabies

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: For droplet precautions, when must staff wear a mask?
questions.rationale: Under droplet precautions, a mask is worn when working within 3 feet of the client.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Droplet Precautions (PDF p. 36)
questions.quote: Wear a mask if working within 3 feet of the client

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In color-coded waste segregation, which container receives infectious items?
questions.rationale: Yellow is for infectious waste; black non-biodegradable, green biodegradable, orange radioactive, red sharps.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Disposal of Equipment (PDF p. 37)
questions.quote: Yellow — infectious items

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which item needs NO special precautions after use by an infected client?
questions.rationale: Dishes require no special precautions; specimens go in leak-proof biohazard containers, sharps in puncture-resistant containers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Disposal of Equipment (PDF p. 37)
questions.quote: Require no special precautions

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Accumulation of carbon dioxide in the blood is called:
questions.rationale: Hypercapnia is CO2 accumulation; hypoxemia is low blood oxygen.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Respiratory Alterations (PDF p. 37)
questions.quote: Hypercapnia — accumulation of carbon dioxide in the blood

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should pursed-lip breathing be done?
questions.rationale: Purse the lips as if to whistle and breathe out slowly without puffing the cheeks.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pursed-Lip Breathing (PDF p. 37)
questions.quote: breathe out slowly and gently without puffing out the cheeks

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In controlled coughing, why cough twice?
questions.rationale: The first cough loosens mucus; the second expels it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Controlled Coughing (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: First cough loosens the mucus, while the second expels the secretions

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the usual sequence for chest physiotherapy?
questions.rationale: The sequence is postural drainage, percussion, vibration, then removal of secretions by coughing or suctioning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Percussion, Vibration and Postural Drainage (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: The sequence for PVD is usually postural drainage, percussion, vibration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Over which area is chest percussion AVOIDED?
questions.rationale: Percussion is avoided over the breasts, sternum, spinal column, and kidneys.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Percussion (PDF p. 38)
questions.quote: Percussion is avoided over the breasts, sternum, spinal column and kidneys

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When is vibration applied during chest physiotherapy?
questions.rationale: Vibrate during exhalation and stop when the client inhales.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vibration (PDF p. 39)
questions.quote: Stop vibrating when the client inhales

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When is postural drainage BEST scheduled?
questions.rationale: Best times are before breakfast, before lunch, late afternoon, and before bedtime, to avoid vomiting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Postural Drainage (PDF p. 39)
questions.quote: Best time includes before breakfast. lunch, in the late afternoon and before bedtime

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which blanket should be used for a client on oxygen?
questions.rationale: Avoid static-generating wool and synthetic fabrics; use cotton.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oxygen Safety (PDF p. 39)
questions.quote: Cotton blankets should be used

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What oxygen concentration does a nasal cannula deliver at 2–6 L/min?
questions.rationale: A nasal cannula delivers 24–45% oxygen at 2–6 L/min.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oxygen Delivery (PDF p. 39)
questions.quote: Delivers relatively low concentration of 02 (24-45%) at flow rates of 2-6 L/min
